title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20); we report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, audited provider-call accounting, artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and pointers to the archived execution bundle for full per-file provenance.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and higher-order safety and policy constraints. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports advocate such workflow-centred mitigations [1]–[3], but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution. Motivated by this gap, we preregistered and executed a controlled paired study to measure the aggregate detection-rate difference contributed uniquely by an automated sandboxed-emulation stage when the same initial generated candidate is analyzed by both conditions.

Research question and contributions. Our preregistered research question was: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete run accounting; (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation explaining a near-zero marginal effect in the chosen regime; (4) concise reproducibility pointers to the archived execution bundle and prescriptive boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Recent survey and architectural reports document the practical trend of combining LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance for NetOps artifacts [1]–[4]. These works emphasize that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional: syntactic parsing, command-ordering/workflow constraints, invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties may each require different V&V primitives. Tool-focused case studies highlight the evolution and limits of static verifiers: configuration-analysis systems have expanded topology-aware checks but still exhibit gaps for runtime-dependent behaviors and stateful sequences [2].

Empirical and prototype evidence. Prototype systems that integrate generation with verification and execution harnesses report heterogeneous gains: in some task regimes a verifier catches most dangerous errors, while in others emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures or environment-specific side effects that static rules miss [2], [5]. These observations motivated our paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation or repair) from generation variability.

Evaluation needs. Surveys and system reports call for workflow-centred benchmarks that combine generation, static verification, and executable validation, but large-scale paired estimates of marginal guarded-stage benefits are scarce. Our study supplies a narrowly scoped, artifact-grounded datapoint in that evaluation agenda.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic missingness handling (reseed up to two times for parser failures; deterministic replacement for irrecoverable failures), multiplicity handling for exploratory secondary tests, and contamination controls based on deterministic hashing and artifact-version checks. Planned confirmatory Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440); planned minimum effect-of-interest for power planning = 0.20.

Task generation and topology templates. Confirmatory items were generated deterministically from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 task family. The bank covers three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest contains initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (make-before-break, must-be-down-for-fields, minimum_active_in_groups). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance after deterministic reseeds. In the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720.

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses). The preregistration enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair we obtained a single sampled initial candidate (one provider call) and that identical candidate was presented to both downstream conditions (baseline and guarded). This isolates downstream guarded-stage effects by removing generation variability as a source of between-condition discordance.

Validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 is a deterministic rule-based checker: vendor-CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, required-sequence and ordering checks, group-level activity constraints, protected-interface invariants, and final-state conformance. The validator emits a binary detection flag and a validator_trace object (validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes). The guarded pipeline runs the validator and then executes the same candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands on vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The emulation harness records runtime observations (interface admin transitions and concurrency, MTU/VLAN application effects, and observable connectivity) and maps selected runtime observations to guarded detections when they reveal policy or safety violations not encoded in the static validator rule set.

Provider-call audit fields and reconciliation (explicit clarification). The archived provider-call audit records model-call events and associates them with coarse stage labels. Two audit fields are central: (a) stage_counts enumerates model-call events by stage label (for this run: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1), and (b) condition_counts enumerates how many provider-call events are associated with the audit labels named "shared" and "guarded" in the run metadata. These fields are not per-condition episode tallies; rather they enumerate provider-call events by role. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the initial shared generation is a single provider call per pair (counted under the stage label that the audit uses for shared initial-generation) and repair-stage calls (if any) are counted under the repair/guarded labels. The observed asymmetry in condition_counts (e.g., a large shared_initial count and a small guarded/repair count) therefore reflects the staged provider-call accounting (one shared initial call per pair plus a small number of repair calls), while complete_pair_count = 720 remains the paired episode count. Deterministic reconciliation verifies consistency between episode accounting and provider-call auditing.

Repair policy and run accounting. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task; repair is permitted only after baseline validator and emulation observations for the guarded condition. Provider-call auditing for the confirmatory execution records model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1; thus only a single repair-stage call occurred across the entire confirmatory set. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, any discordant pair (guarded-only detection) must be attributable to either an emulation-observed runtime violation or to that single repair invocation; both are traceable in the archived per-episode artifacts via the canonical execution manifest.

Analysis procedures. The primary analysis used a paired-binary executor aligned with McNemar-style inference and produced a two-sided exact McNemar p-value plus a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) for the paired difference (guarded − baseline). Secondary exploratory per-class and per-vendor paired analyses were pre-specified and treated with multiplicity adjustments in the preregistration. The primary analysis used complete-pair handling because there were no irrecoverable technical pairs in the confirmatory run.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inferential statistics (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency counts were: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values reported here are verbatim from the preregistered analysis executor outputs.

Contingency summary (compact). - Npairs = 720 (complete paired episodes)
- Baseline successes = 719; Baseline success rate = 0.9986111111111111
- Guarded successes = 720; Guarded success rate = 1.0
- Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884
- Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0
- 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667] (10000 resamples, seed = 1729)

Discordant-pair attribution and repair accounting. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation identify a single repair-stage invocation and the single n10 discordant count. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the permissible causes for that guarded-only detection are: (i) an emulation observation not encoded as a validator violation, or (ii) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The canonical execution manifest archived with the run contains the complete per-episode raw results, validator traces, emulation observations, and repair-call transcripts that allow an auditor to locate and inspect that unique discordant pair. The run-level accounting reported above (model_calls_used = 721; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720; repair = 1) reconciles with complete_pair_count = 720 under the provider-call audit semantics described in Methods.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative scoring traces include validator_trace objects with normalized_configuration, validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count. Those representative artifacts illustrate that the overwhelming majority of shared_initial candidates complied with validator rules (violation_count = 0) and that sandboxed emulation largely corroborated validator findings in this curated task bank.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded factors that explain the near-zero aggregate effect and define practical boundary conditions where guarded stages are—and are not—likely to matter.

1) Validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator explicitly encodes the syntactic and workflow checks exercised by the curated tasks (examples: shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). The very high baseline success rate (719/720) leaves essentially no headroom for the guarded stage to flag additional failures in this constrained regime.

2) Curated inclusion and reduced adversarial exposure. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated and required parser acceptance before inclusion. This filtering concentrated the sample on parser-validated, policy-constrained scenarios; runtime-only faults that emulation exposes in broader or adversarial sets are therefore underrepresented here.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. Reusing the exact sampled initial candidate for both baseline and guarded conditions isolates downstream signals as the only source of discordance. The single observed discordant pair corresponds to the single recorded repair-stage call or to an emulation-only observation; the archived artifacts permit direct inspection of that mapping.

Operational implications. For environments with a high-coverage static validator tailored to expected intent patterns and with strong input prevalidation, adding an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may yield negligible incremental detection benefit at scale. This should not be generalized beyond the examined regime. Guarded sandboxing remains valuable for (a) noisy natural-language intents, (b) adversarially crafted misconfigurations, (c) broader vendor-CLI diversity, or (d) longer-lived stateful procedures where runtime semantics matter.

Practical recommendations. The artifacts suggest three pragmatic paths: (i) invest in richer static validators when low-latency, high-throughput intent→config translation is required; (ii) deploy guarded sandboxing selectively for high-impact changes where emulation fidelity matters; (iii) use adversarial/fuzzing task banks to identify validator gaps—the archived run contains representative traces that can seed such adversarial case generation.

Limitations tied to the archived evidence. The near-zero aggregate effect is specific to the preregistered task bank, single validator implementation, declared/requested model, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study was powered a priori for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and must be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than as a general negative result for all NetOps workflows. Emulation fidelity and cross-vendor generality remain open questions.
sections.conclusion:
We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows a single repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification that the discordance is localized and auditable via the canonical execution manifest. We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design; follow-up work should focus on adversarial and production-like task banks, multi-validator ensembles, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages add substantive operational value.

Reproducibility pointer (compact). The archived canonical execution manifest and analysis artifacts contain the full per-file provenance, raw per-episode results, validator traces, emulation observations, and repair transcripts. See the canonical execution manifest in the archived bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json) for the complete artifact index and per-file locations required for independent verification. The manifest enumerates the raw results, reconciliation outputs, and analysis artifacts used to produce the numeric results reported above.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived manifest and reconciliation artifacts.
